questions.text: I read “s009 accept” as: only “Keep the Adult Part of Yourself in Charge” becomes an h2, so it now sits under “The Most Extreme Example” as its lesson, and that heading and “Reversing Accidental Affirmations” stay h1. Right, or did you mean both S008 and S009 under “Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists”?

“Hypnosis-specific audit” joins “Find a Hypnotist Who Fits” in Appendix F: your three lists first, as they are, then your audit, as it is, then your “firmly encouraged” line and your “Then afterwards” paragraph. Two changes: “interview them a bit:” becomes “interview them a bit more:”, since your three lists now come first; “After it’s over, check how well your critical thinking is working when you look back on how it went.” joins the start of your “Then afterwards” paragraph. The audit as it would read there:

Before you let a hypnotic recording or a live hypnotist put manipulative suggestions into your skull, interview them a bit more:

First, what are they going to do to bring you under? And if you react negatively to something, will they pause to change the script? Make sure they are fine with stopping the whole thing.

And how are they deciding it's working? Just because you seem "out of it" shouldn't be a green light. Are they using sneaky moves to get past your adult judgement, like putting you into identity roles (including age regression)? Walking you down obedience ladders? Your desire for belonging also shouldn't be used for that.

Keep in mind though, you can only answer those last questions by reading the script first. You can't expect them to know what your adult judgement would accept, so make that clear ahead of time.

Will they tell you before they use techniques that affect your memory or behaviors after the session? Like fractionation or cues.

Are they low-key using your body signals to prove their theories? Like oh your hand dropped real fast, so you ARE gay.

And when it's time to come out, will they tell you clearly that the session is over, so you get your normal waking, walking self back?

If any answer they give you is wishy washy, beware. Ask for the exact script (or the methods used since they probably aren't exactly reading a script). If they don't want to give the secrets away, walk right out that door.

Keep it like this, or tell me what to change.

“The General Rule” goes, and this sentence ends “Could It Be Psychosis?”, linked:
The general rule is the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”: if what you're doing is making you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated or scared, or things feel more and more unreal, stop going deeper and get help.
It keeps every warning sign of yours; the first half of your rule (more loving, grounded, relational, honest, functional) is what the linked section says.

After your line under “Keep Daydreaming?”, the same pointer you use under “Getting Anxious?”:
Sit up and open your eyes, and ask yourself, “What are you avoiding doing in the real world by doing this?” For more on daydreaming, see Appendix E.

With the “Appendices” heading goes its note (“Note: You can skip this section and just use the main path. This is additional info to help you be more precise and safe, and some additional scripts for other situations.”), since your first section already says there are lots of appendices with extra tools. With “Appendix I: Sleep hypnosis” goes its line (“For sleep, try using this playlist by Nimja .”): “Sleep Induction” links the same Nimja playlist. J and K become I and J, and “All sources used are in Appendix K” becomes “Appendix J”.

The guide didn't mention Systema anywhere yet. After your Buteyko lines, this, with its two links (the video you named as the best, and the Systema section of your somatic post):
Try Systema's continuous breathing too: besides relaxing you, it can take you deeper into trance and flow states. This is the best video on it I've seen so far, and my somatic guide explains it more.
The proposal for its heading is now “Buteyko & Systema”, so the sidebar names both. Keep it like this, or tell me what to change.
